Event Cinema | Barbican

# Event Cinema 

The best of the stage – be it opera, theatre or dance – and must-see art exhibitions broadcast straight to our cinemas.

From New York's Metropolitan Opera to Stage Russia, the Royal Ballet to the National Theatre, enjoy the best stage craft and visit the best art museums from around the world, all from the comfort of our cinemas. 

## Events

## NT Live: Les Liaisons Dangereuses

 Thu 25 Jun 2026, 19:30 

Lesley Manville (Phantom Thread) joins Aidan Turner (Rivals) in a striking new staging of the classic novel, where amongst the glittering salons one misstep can mean ruin.

## MET Opera Live in HD: El Último Sueño de Frida y Diego

 Sat 30 May 2026, 18:00 

A live transmission of American composer Gabriela Lena Frank’s first opera – a magical-realist portrait of Mexico’s painterly power couple Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera – with libretto by Nilo Cruz.

## NT Live: The Playboy of the Western World

 Thu 28 May 2026, 18:00 

This riveting story of youth and self-discovery turns Pegeen Flaherty's life upside down after a man walks into her pub claiming he's killed his father.

## Power To The People: John & Yoko Live in NYC

 Sun 3 May 2026, 14:00 

The newly restored live shows by John Lennon & Yoko Ono at Madison Square Garden in 1972 is a witness of the couple as political radicals in New York City.

## MET Opera Live: Eugene Onegin

 Sat 2 May 2026, 18:00 

This ardent operatic adaptation of Pushkin, is a lyrical romance between Tatiana and Onegin. 

## RBO Live: The Magic Flute

 Tue 21 Apr 2026, 18:45 

A star cast leads Mozart's fantastical opera in David McVicar's enchanting production. 

## NT Live: All My Sons

 Thu 16 Apr 2026, 18:00 

Bryan Cranston and Marianne Jean-Baptiste feature in a triumphantly acclaimed new production of Arthur Miller’s classic play, from visionary director Ivo Van Hove. 

## RBO Live: Siegfried

 Tue 31 Mar 2026, 17:15 

Moments of transcendent beauty and heroic triumph sparkle in the third chapter of Wagner’s Ring cycle, brought to life under Barrie Kosky’s inspired eye and a score conducted by Antonio Pappano.

## RBO Live: Giselle

 Sun 22 Mar 2026, 19:15 

Peter Wright’s atmospheric and bewitching production of the quintessential Romantic ballet.

## MET Opera Live: Tristan und Isolde

 Sat 21 – Sun 22 Mar 2026 

Wagner's transcendent meditation on love and death is brought to life after years of anticipation.

## NT Live: The Audience

 Thu 26 Feb 2026, 19:15 

Returning to cinemas for the first time in over a decade, Helen Mirren plays Queen Elizabeth II in the Olivier and Tony Award-winning hit production, directed by Stephen Daldry.

## RBO Live: Woolf Works

 Sun 15 Feb 2026, 14:00 

This immense work is inspired by the iconic writer, Virginia Woolf, capturing the heart of her uniquely artistic spirit. 

## NT Live: Hamlet

 Thu 22 Jan 2026, 19:00 

This fearless, contemporary take on Shakespeare's famous tragedy stars Hiran Abeysekera (Life of Pi) as the brooding Prince of Denmark.

## RBO Live: La Traviata

 Sun 18 Jan 2026, 14:00 

Richard Eyre’s beautiful production provides the perfect setting for Verdi's opera about a courtesan who sacrifices all for love.

## MET Opera Live in HD: I Puritani

 Sat 10 Jan 2026, 18:00 

Lisette Oropesa and Lawrence Brownlee star in Bellini's final opera – a passionate love story set during the English Civil War.

## RBO Live: The Nutcracker

 Sun 14 Dec 2025, 14:00 

The enchanting ballet features Tchaikovsky's most familiar melodies and is bought to life with exquisite designs. 

## MET Opera Live: Andrea Chénier

 Sat 13 Dec 2025, 18:00 

Giordano's passionate tragedy set against the backdrop of the violence and intrigue of the French Revolution.

## RBO Live: Cinderella

 Sun 30 Nov 2025, 14:00 

This Winter, be transported into an ethereal world where a sprinkling of fairy dust makes dreams come true.

## NT Live: The Fifth Step

 Thu 27 Nov 2025, 18:20 

Olivier Award-winner Jack Lowden is joined by Emmy and BAFTA-winner Martin Freeman starring in the critically acclaimed and subversively funny new play by David Ireland.

## MET Opera Live in HD: Arabella

 Sat 22 Nov 2025, 18:00 

A romantic comedy opera about love and money, as a family faces financial ruin in the extravagant society of 19th-century Vienna.

Location Barbican Cinema 1 is located within the main Barbican building on Level -2. Head to Level G and walk towards the Lakeside Terrace where you’ll find stairs and lifts to take you down to the venue floor. Address Barbican Centre Silk Street, London EC2Y 8DS

Public transport The Barbican is widely accessible by bus, tube, train and by foot or bicycle. Plan your journey and find more route information in ‘ Your Visit’ or book your car parking space in advance.

Location Barbican Cinema 2 & 3 are located on Beech Street, a short walk from the Barbican’s Silk Street entrance. From Silk Street, you’ll see a zebra crossing that will take you over the road to the venue. Address Beech Street, London EC2Y 8DS

Nearby public transport We are within walking distance from a number of London Underground stations, the closest being Barbican, St Paul’s and Moorgate. The nearest train stations are Liverpool Street and Farringdon. Bus Route 153 runs directly past the Barbican along Chiswell Street

Car and bicycle parking We have free bicycle spaces and paid car parking spaces available

Access Level access from the Pit floor foyer only to the two boxes (see Mobility below). All other seats lead off stepped aisles.

Mobility Two boxes at the rear of the auditorium each have space for one wheelchair user and a companion. Please book early and ask for these seats.

Assistance dogs Assistance dogs may be taken into the cinema – please tell us when booking, to ensure your seat has enough space. If you prefer, you may leave your dog with a member of the foyer staff during the performance.

Hearing facility There is an induction loop in the auditorium. You can use this by adjusting your hearing aid to the ‘T’ setting.

For more access information, please visit our Accessibility section.

Access Cinemas 2 & 3 are located at Beech Street, a short walk from the Barbican Centre’s main Silk Street entrance. There are a couple of steep, dropped kerbs and an incline to negotiate between the two sites. Level access from Beech Street.

Mobility Each auditorium has three permanent wheelchair spaces (two in the third row and one in the front row) and 153 fixed seats with capacity for a further three spaces in the front row. Access to each auditorium is up a ramp. There are also a number of seats with step-free access.

Assistance dogs Assistance dogs may be taken into the cinema – please tell us when booking to ensure your seat has enough space. If you prefer, you may leave your dog with a member of the foyer staff during the performance.

Hearing facility An infrared system for hard of hearing customers is provided in each auditorium; headsets or neck loops can be collected from foyer staff. The ticket desk counter is fitted with an induction loop.

For more access information, please visit our Accessibility section.
